heroHeadline: All Flotilla Activists Deported as IPS Defends Ben-Gvir Video; IDF Extends Death Penalty to West Bank
heroSubtitle: All approximately 430 Gaza aid flotilla activists from 19+ countries were deported by May 22, 2026, as the Israel Prison Service formally declared that all conduct shown in National Security Minister Ben-Gvir's viral abuse video was carried out 'in accordance with procedures.' The UK joined 15+ nations that have now summoned Israeli ambassadors, while EU member states continued pursuing unprecedented personal sanctions against a sitting Israeli minister. In a separate legal escalation, IDF Central Command Chief Maj. Gen. Avi Bluth signed an order extending Israel's death penalty provisions to Palestinian civilians in the occupied West Bank. Prime Minister Netanyahu publicly rebuked Ben-Gvir's conduct while affirming Israel's right to enforce its Gaza naval blockade. ICC Pre-Trial Chamber I continues reviewing warrant applications for Ben-Gvir, Smotrich, Strock, and two IDF officials — with the Smotrich application reportedly the first-ever ICC warrant to include an apartheid charge. The Gaza death toll stands at 72,800+ documented since October 7, 2023, with 930+ killed since the October 2025 ceasefire and Netanyahu's cabinet admission that Israel controls 60% of Gaza — beyond the agreed Yellow Line.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OCHA, IDF, Gaza Ministry of Health, B'Tselem, ICC, ICJ, Reuters, Al Jazeera, OHCHR, UNRWA, Times of Israel, Haaretz, Bloomberg, Jerusalem Post, Human Rights Watch, Save the Children, Amnesty International, UNICEF, NPR, Middle East Eye, CNN, The National, Euronews, CBC News, and institutional analyses. Casualty figures are subject to ongoing verification. The conflict has persisted since Israeli independence on May 14, 1948.
